hook.line: A good conclusion does not just repeat what you said. It also says what is still open, and Spanish has a neat way to do that in one short phrase.
hook.es: Queda por resolver si el efecto se mantiene a largo plazo.
hook.en: It remains to be established whether the effect lasts in the long term.

examples.es: Queda por resolver si el efecto se mantiene a largo plazo.
examples.en: It remains to be established whether the effect lasts in the long term.

examples.es: Quedan por estudiar los casos rurales.
examples.en: The rural cases are yet to be studied.

examples.es: Queda por decidir quién pagará el arreglo.
examples.en: It remains to be decided who will pay for the repair.

examples.es: Queda por ver si Altamira cumple su palabra.
examples.en: It remains to be seen whether Altamira keeps its word.

examples.es: Quedan por explicar las causas del problema.
examples.en: The causes of the problem are yet to be explained.
There is still a lot to do.

rule:
*Queda(n) por* + infinitive names what is still unfinished. English needs a passive ("remains to be solved"); Spanish keeps the plain infinitive: *queda por resolver*.

*Queda* agrees with the thing left over: *queda por decidir el precio*, *quedan por estudiar los casos*. When a question follows (*si*, *quién*, *cómo*), it is one idea, so *queda* stays singular: *queda por ver si…*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this *quedar por* + infinitive. It has a passive meaning even though the infinitive looks active.

options: The problem has been solved.
The problem remains to be solved.
The problems remain to be solved.
The doubts remain to be resolved.
The doubt remains to be resolved.
The doubts were resolved.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *queda* or *quedan* and type the whole sentence: *___ por estudiar los casos rurales.*
yourTurn.answer: Quedan por estudiar los casos rurales.
yourTurn.why: The cases are plural, so *queda* becomes *quedan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It remains to be decided who will pay for the repair.
yourTurn.answer: Queda por decidir quién pagará el arreglo.
yourTurn.why: A question after *queda por* counts as one idea, so *queda* stays singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The causes are yet to be explained.
accept: Quedan por explicar las causas del problema.
yourTurn.why: Several causes left over, so *quedan*, then the plain infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It remains to be seen whether Altamira keeps its word.
yourTurn.answer: Queda por ver si Altamira cumple su palabra.
yourTurn.why: *Queda por ver si…* is the Spanish way to say "it remains to be seen whether".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: There is still a lot to do.
yourTurn.why: *Mucho* is singular here, so the verb is *queda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Queda por resolver un problema.* Say: Two problems remain to be solved.
yourTurn.why: Two problems means *quedan*; the infinitive does not change.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Several questions remain to be answered.
yourTurn.why: The questions are plural, so *quedan* comes with *por responder*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The verb agrees with what is left, and there is one problem.

pitfalls.wrong: Queda por ser resuelto el problema.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish keeps a plain infinitive here; no *ser* + participle is needed.

pitfalls.wrong: Queda a resolver si el efecto dura.
pitfalls.right: Queda por resolver si el efecto dura.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase always uses *por*, not *a*.

personal: Say one thing that is still open in your life right now, starting with *Queda por*.
